item.text: I’m checking the highest-value independent analyses first and separating direct Putin attribution from broader commentary. If a page is only a thin rehash of another family, I’ll reject it as duplicate or weak rather than pad the set.

The New START and Belarus analyses are opening cleanly. I’m now checking whether the remaining items add distinct content or just restate the same two families: suspension of arms control and Belarus-based nuclear coercion.

## Remaining Gaps
- `1B.7` is still thin. I still do not have strong ruler-specific evidence on whether Putin surrounded nuclear/security decisions with experts versus loyalists.
- `1B.9` remains weak. I have general digital/cyber and AI governance references elsewhere, but not much that directly links Putin’s 2023 choices to catastrophic-risk handling in those domains.
- The direct Kremlin transcript for the Feb. 21 New START speech remains absent in this wave, so the record still leans on secondary citations of the speech.
- The Belarus deployment chain is now much better covered, but I still lack a clean primary custody/command document showing the exact operational handoff, if any.
- The set now has good adverse coverage and some conditional de-escalation evidence, but the “best available” balance still points heavily toward escalation, leverage, and arms-control erosion.
